entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad

sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another Counsel for Applicant :- Kamal Kishor Mishra Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Subhash Chandra Sharma,J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. for the State.

The present anticipatory bail application under Section 438 Cr.P.C. has been moved seeking bail in Case Crime No.70 of 2016, under Sections 498A, 420, 323 IPC, Police Station Mahila Thana,
District Meerut.
It is submitted by the learned counsel for the applicant that in this case applicant and informant are husband and wife.
There was dispute between both the parties relating to which an F.I.R. was lodged by the informant/wife against the applicant, his brother and mother.
It is further submitted that during investigation interim anticipatory bail was granted in favour of the applicant and charge-sheet was submitted after conclusion of investigation in the year 2017.

It is also submitted that the aforesaid charge-sheet was challenged before this Court by the applicant which was disposed of with a direction to the applicant to move discharge application before the learned trial Lokesh vs State Of U.P. And Another on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71815063/
1 court.

sentences.text: In pursuance of which he applied an application for discharge which was rejected by the learned Court.

Again he came before this Court by moving an application under Section 482 Cr.P.C.
in which matter was referred to the mediation which was succeeded even though the opposite party did not agree to live with the applicant and entered into marriage with some other person.
Now, in pursuance of process of the court there is apprehension of arrest against the applicant so requested for anticipatory bail.

Learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer for anticipatory bail and urged that in this case the offences said to have been committed by the applicant are punishable with sentence less than seven years and in which there may be no apprehension of arrest against the applicant by the police.

Further urged that after investigation the charge-sheet was submitted before the learned Court in the year 2017 and since then applicant is not appearing before the learned trial court, therefore, he is not entitled for anticipatory bail.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and from the perusal of record, it appears that charge-sheet was submitted in the year 2017 which was challenged before this Court unsuccessfully.

The discharge application moved by the applicant was also rejected by the learned trial Court even though he is not appearing before it but avoiding the process of the court, therefore, in such a situation there appears no ground for anticipatory bail in favour of the applicant.
Hence, the anticipatory bail application of the applicant is, hereby, rejected.

However, it is directed that in case, the applicant appears and moves bail application before the learned court concerned, it will be heard and decided expeditiously as far as possible in the light of law as laid down in the case of Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and another LL 2021 SC 550, decided by Hon'ble the Supreme Court.
